## c4e70c48d698

**Disposition: No issue found in generated data after checking.** Generator SHA-256 `71e6fabeb764b4cc8530f15cb66bfeab46cbc913643a1e522e3882a28539bc4a` was left unchanged.

I ran the full 12-stage after-policy battery. Eleven stages were green; `semantic_gate` was the only non-green stage because the after policy treats semantic warnings as blocking. The gate sampled 600/600 strict inputs, accepted 3/3 canonical examples, observed all 11/11 witnesses, verified all 6/6 declared rival claims, and found all 12/12 sampled lessons identifiable. Override rejection and Racket execution parity passed.

The warning is an **evidence gap**, not a reproduced label or lesson defect: five witnesses—`distance_0_seed`, `distance_3plus_layer`, `branched_contact_graph`, `cyclic_contact_graph`, and `same_shape_different_layers`—declare no `WITNESS_RIVALS` claim. Their frequency proves those features occur, but not that a named shortcut changes an answer there. Evidence: `checks/audit-targets/c4e70c48d698/checks/c4e70c48d698_after_semantic_gate.log` and battery summary `checks/audit-targets/c4e70c48d698/checks/c4e70c48d698_after_battery_summary.json`.

I did not invent a counterexample from the missing claims. A useful future improvement would be to pair each weak witness with a concrete executable rival, or explicitly classify it as coverage-only so the semantic gate can distinguish coverage evidence from shortcut evidence.
